Reminder: this offering is closing.

At the launch of its new GPT-6 “Astra” model this month, OpenAI president Greg Brockman made a bold declaration: the “AGI era” has begun.¹

In plain terms, AGI refers to AI that can match or surpass humans across virtually every cognitive task. OpenAI’s own bar is systems that “outperform humans at most economically valuable work.”¹, ²

OpenAI calls Astra its “most intelligent and aligned” model yet. In one demo, it finished a job search in under three minutes that OpenAI said would take a person roughly five hours.²

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang put it plainly: “AGI has arrived.”¹

To be clear, there’s no agreed-upon definition of AGI, and researchers caution that no single benchmark proves we’ve crossed the line.¹, ²

But step back from the semantics, and one thing is clear: amid fierce competition with Anthropic and other rivals, OpenAI is still one of the leading names pushing AI forward.

There’s no guarantee that OpenAI’s technology, revenue, or valuation will continue to grow, or that the company will be profitable. See the risk disclosures on the offering page.
